      "id": "D001",
      "name": "NumStability.FirstOrderEquation.admissibleStates",
      "interpretation": "Projects the equation's stored set of real vector states.",
      "effect_on_target": "Restricts the hyperbolicity test and requires both initial states to belong to this set.",
      "source_match": "A state domain is reasonable for nonlinear equations, but the selected passage does not specify this independently supplied set or its relation to the governing equation.",
      "status": "unclear"
    },
    {
      "id": "D002",
      "name": "NumStability.FirstOrderEquation.principal",
      "interpretation": "Projects a matrix-valued function of two real coordinates and a state.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the matrices required to have real eigenbases.",
      "source_match": "Matches A and potentially f'(q), but the supplied declarations do not establish the differential-equation interpretation of an arbitrary such function.",
      "status": "unclear"
    },
    {
      "id": "D003",
      "name": "NumStability.FirstOrderInitialValueProblem",
      "interpretation": "The constructor D011 packages an equation record and a spatial initial-state function.",

    {

    },
    {
      "id": "D006",
      "name": "NumStability.FirstOrderInitialValueProblem.IsRiemannWithStates",
      "interpretation": "Conjoins equation hyperbolicity, membership of both states, and the two strict-half-line data conditions.",

      "source_match": "Preserves equation plus data, but inherits unresolved equation-domain and equal-state conventions.",
      "status": "unclear"
    },
    {
      "id": "D007",
      "name": "NumStability.FirstOrderInitialValueProblem.governing",

      "status": "pass"

      "status": "pass"

    {
      "id": "D009",
      "name": "NumStability.FirstOrderEquation",
      "interpretation": "By D013, stores a state set, a matrix-valued coefficient function, and a vector-valued forcing function.",

      "source_match": "Contains plausible first-order equation data, but no supplied declaration ties the record to a differential equation, and its arbitrary forcing and coordinate dependence extend beyond the displayed homogeneous examples.",

    },
    {
      "id": "D010",
      "name": "NumStability.FirstOrderEquation.IsHyperbolic",

    },
    {
